newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia's Howard doesn't rule out tax hike.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia's Howard doesn't rule out tax hike.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard on Sunday refused to rule out increased taxes to compensate indigenous people if his coalition government legislated to wipe out native title on pastoral leases.
But he added he found the option "monumentally unattractive".
Asked on the Nine television network if he would rule out raising taxes Howard replied:
"...look I'm going to talk to everybody and see if we can reach a common ground, but the idea of increasing taxes for any purpose is monumentally unattractive to me."

National Party president Don McDonald said last week increased taxes would compensate Aborigines for legalislation to extinguish native title. The National Party is the junior partner to Howard's Liberal party in the coalition government.
Howard played down any divisions in the coalition over the response to the High Court's ruling in the Wik case in December that pastoral leases do not automatically over-ride Aboriginal native title.
"No, I don't think there are any divisions," Howard said.

The High Court in a split decision made its ruling on a claim by two Aboriginal groups, the Wik and Thayorre tribes, against an earlier lower court ruling that pastoral leases extinguished native title.
About 40 percent of Australia's land area is under pastoral leases, including many mining and exploration permit areas.
The preamble to the Native Title Act passed by the former Labor government in 1994 said it was intended that pastoral leases should extinguish native title but this was not incorporated in the act.
Farmers and miners say the court's decision has cast a pall of uncertainty over their ability to do anything on leasehold land.
Last week, National Party Leader and Deputy Prime Minister Tim Fischer outlined his party's official position that federal legislation was required to extinguish native title.
A legislative solution has been urged by pastoralists and state governments, but rejected by Aboriginal groups who favour regional negotiations.
People of Aboriginal descent make up less than two percent of Australia's 18 million population.
